clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A unit proposes using the same fixed time interval to discontinue Transmission-Based Precautions for every infectious diagnosis. Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Use the diagnosis-specific precaution type and duration in current CDC guidance rather than one universal interval.
options.B: Use a 24-hour interval for every diagnosis because transmission risk ends at the same point for all infections.
options.C: Require negative cultures before stopping precautions for every diagnosis regardless of the CDC duration guidance.
options.D: Continue every Transmission-Based Precaution indefinitely because duration cannot be estimated by infection type.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC Appendix A assigns infection- and condition-specific precaution types and durations rather than one universal stopping interval. For example, some conditions use precautions for the duration of illness, while others use treatment- and culture-based criteria or case-by-case public-health guidance. Therefore, discontinuation decisions should follow the current pathogen- or condition-specific recommendation and applicable facility/public-health requirements rather than a fixed time or universal negative-culture rule.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Determine when Transmission-Based Precautions may be discontinued by using the current CDC diagnosis-specific duration criteria rather than a universal time or testing rule.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC uses infection- and condition-specific precaution durations; there is no single fixed duration or universal culture-clearance rule that applies to all Transmission-Based Precautions.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, removed the 'all' absolute distractor, and anchored the decision to CDC Appendix A's explicit infection-specific type-and-duration framework.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Transmission-Based Precautions
audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely long and distractors were universal extremes. The revised item directly tests the CDC condition-specific duration framework using balanced policy choices.

option_audit.A: Correct. CDC Appendix A assigns precaution duration by infection or condition rather than one universal interval.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC lists many different duration rules; a single 24-hour rule is not applicable to all infections.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Some diagnoses use culture-based clearance, but many do not; a universal negative-culture rule is unsupported.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC provides defined or case-specific duration criteria rather than indefinite precautions for every diagnosis.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects the structure and purpose of the current CDC Appendix A duration table.
cueing_check: All four choices are policy approaches to discontinuing precautions and are comparable in length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: current CDC Appendix A freshly verified
no universal fixed-time or culture rule introduced
